MMemora /01 · Product overviewProduct Handbook
01
01 · Product overview

What Memora is

Memora is a memory service for other applications. An application registers files, URLs or chat transcripts in a workspace; Memora stores them, reads them with NVIDIA models, splits them into chunks, embeds and indexes them, builds a knowledge graph, and answers questions with cited evidence, scoped so each application sees only its own data.

FIG 01

From upload to answer

each stage runs on request or after the one before it

One ownership chain

Tenant → application → subject → source. Every row knows its owners, so nothing is reachable by ID alone.

Reads hard documents

Per-page triage sends scans, tables and charts to layout and vision models; clean text stays local and free.

Cited, honest answers

Hybrid search, reranking and a grounded prompt; the answer says when the knowledge is insufficient.

Graph RAG, measured

A knowledge graph per tenant, and an Arena and benchmarks that compare it with vector RAG on your own questions.

Key takeaway

Memora is infrastructure, not an end-user app: client applications such as Pingie call its API, and operators manage it from the console.

Who it serves and what it solves

Teams whose applications must remember documents and conversations, without each building its own retrieval stack.

Problem → how Memora responds
Problem

Every application rebuilds parsing, chunking, embeddings and search.

Response

One API covers registration through grounded answers; an application only sends files and questions.

Problem

Simple parsers lose tables, scans and charts.

Response

Hard pages are routed to NVIDIA layout and vision models; every run is versioned with its cost.

Problem

Customer data must never cross between tenants.

Response

A credential resolves to exactly one application; every service call checks ownership and answers 404 otherwise.

Problem

Nobody knows whether Graph RAG is worth its cost.

Response

The Arena and benchmarks score vector, graph and hybrid pipelines on the same questions.

Who uses which part
Uses
Client applicationsThe REST API with a memora_… token
OperatorsThe console, signed in with Google
IntegratorsThe public site's API reference

02 · Core concepts

The ownership chain

Everything in Memora hangs off one chain. Reading it top to bottom is the whole data model.

FIG 02

The ownership chain

README · db/models

An actor is not a subject

The actor caused a workspace to exist; the subject is the workspace.

Ownership is derived

A source's tenant and application are copied from its subject, never sent by the client.

The chain must agree

A source asked for under the wrong subject is not found, even when you own both.

Not an identity provider

An actor stores only your external_id: no email, password or role.

Registering sources

A source is one piece of registered knowledge inside a subject. Files are stored; URLs and chats can be recorded as metadata only.

Implemented

Upload a file

Any type up to 50 MiB. extract=true starts reading straight away; build_graph=true adds the graph.

Implemented

Register a URL or chat

A row that points at content stored elsewhere; no bytes move.

Implemented

Folders

Subjects nest by parent; moves and subtree deletes are checked with recursive queries.

Safe write and delete order
01

Check scope

The subject must belong to the caller.

02

Write bytes

Original file to local disk or Cloudflare R2.

03

Write the row

If it fails, the bytes are removed again.

Purpose

Give every file a tracked, owned identity before any processing.

How it behaves

The client never sends tenant or application ids; they are copied from the subject in the path.

Why it matters

A caller cannot attach a file to data it does not own.

Limits

No file-type allow-list; the size limit applies only when the upload's size is known.

Extraction Agent: reading documents

Local parsers decide which pages are hard; only hard parts go to NVIDIA models. Each run is a new version, with every model call and its cost recorded.

FIG 03

Per-page triage

PDF pages; other types route by kind
RoleDefault model
layoutnvidia/nemotron-parse
visionnemotron-3-nano-omni-30b
extract · answer · graphnemotron-3-super-120b
  • Reads PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images and plain text.
  • Deep mode sends every PDF page to the layout model.
  • Up to 30 pages per document; 4 calls in parallel by default.
  • Fallback: layout → vision → local text; some units failed means partial.
Key takeaway

Extraction keeps the per-page readings and the merged text, so chunking and the graph never pay to read the document again.

MMemora /03 · FeaturesProduct Handbook
03 · Features

Chunking

Chunking is local and free. It turns an extraction's readings into retrieval-sized pieces that follow the document's own structure.

FIG 04

Chunking stages

app/chunking
Target size300–500tokens
Soft max600tokens
Hard max1,200tokens
Overlap0by default
Purpose

Make pieces that answer one thing each, with their place in the document.

How it behaves

Runs after every successful extraction, or on POST /sources/{id}/rechunk. A new version becomes active and older ones switch off in one transaction.

Why it matters

Chunks can be rebuilt at will, without model cost, and every answer can name its section.

Limits

A coherent section under 300 tokens stays small: chunks are never padded.

MMemora /03 · FeaturesProduct Handbook
03 · Features

Embeddings and strategies

Each chunk is embedded into pgvector under a strategy, indexed with HNSW, and kept in step with the chunks.

ModelStrategy
What it isA physical embedding modelHow Memora uses it
Examplenvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b, 2,048 dims“Memora Dense v1”, seeded by migration
HoldsDimensions, normalisationInput field, templates, normalisation, metric
Changes—Immutable; a different setup is a new strategy
Key takeaway

Because strategies never change, every vector knows exactly what produced it, and several strategies can be compared side by side.

Idempotent

A hash of strategy, model and exact text: unchanged content re-embeds as a no-op and spends nothing.

Tracked and retried

Each vector goes pending → processing → completed or failed, retried up to 3 times with the error kept.

Coverage you can see

The Embeddings page shows total, embedded and processing chunks, coverage, and the strategies.

Ask Memora: retrieval and grounded answers

A question is answered only from chunks the caller owns. Two searches are fused, diversified and reranked; the model then answers from the best six, citing them.

FIG 05

Query pipeline

default sizes from config.py
  1. 1
    Scope itOptional subject, source or strategy narrows the search; none means everything you own.
  2. 2
    See every stageThe response traces how many candidates each stage kept, with similarity and rerank scores.
  3. 3
    Stream it/query/stream sends the evidence first, then answer text, then token usage.
Scope note

The answer is generated by the LLM from the chunks; whether each sentence is supported is not checked on this path. The unified Graph RAG pipeline does check citations.

The knowledge graph

An NVIDIA model reads each extraction for entities and relationships from a fixed ontology. Facts land in one FalkorDB graph per tenant, each pointing back to its source and chunk.

FIG 06

Knowledge graph build

app/graph
Ontology v1 · 10 entity types
PERSONORGANIZATIONCOMPANYPRODUCTLOCATIONTECHNOLOGYPROJECTDOCUMENTCONCEPTEVENT
20 relation types, e.g.
WORKS_FORMANAGESOWNSUSESSUPPLIESPARTY_TOLOCATED_INPART_OFDEPENDS_ONRELATED_TO

Unknown types fall back to CONCEPT and RELATED_TO, keeping the original label.

Purpose

Capture who and what documents mention, and how they relate.

How it behaves

Built on request per source. A subject's view is filtered to facts from its own sources and subfolders. Retrieval follows 1–3 deterministic hops.

Why it matters

Relationship questions can use connected facts, not just similar text.

Limits

Optional: without a FalkorDB URL, graph endpoints answer 503 and everything else works.

MMemora /03 · FeaturesProduct Handbook
03 · Features

Graph RAG and the Arena

Graph RAG runs as its own service beside vector RAG. The console's Arena asks one question of each pipeline and shows the answers, evidence, time and cost side by side.

FIG 07

Arena pipelines

docs/graph-rag-compare.md
Five graph techniques

spreading

Multi-seed spreading activation with hop decay.

ppr

Personalised PageRank around the question.

dual_level

LightRAG-style entity and theme matching.

paths

Shortest paths between seed entities, as chains.

community

Question against community summaries.

Key takeaway

Embedding similarity can't tell a match from a near-miss here, so “nothing relevant” is decided by the reranker: a best score under −5.0 is flagged as weak evidence.

Benchmarks, Advisor and Source inspector

Three tools turn the comparison into evidence: score pipelines on many questions, weigh the trade-offs, and check how one file's graph was built.

Benchmarks/compare/benchmarks
  • Runs pipelines over a question set, loaded from a file.
  • Scored against expected answers and supporting chunks.
  • Scorecard, per-question wins and losses, results by question type.
  • Shows set-up cost: Graph RAG spends effort before any question.
Advisorreads a benchmark
  • Weights accuracy, cost per question and explainability.
  • Compares vector RAG with the best graph pipeline per question type.
  • Says whether a lead is bigger than the noise for that many questions.
  • Explainability is a property of the method, not a measurement.
Source inspector/compare/inspect
  • One file's graph beside the passages it came from.
  • Each passage shows the entities and facts it produced.
  • Flags weak extraction: empty passages, isolated entities, low-confidence facts.
  • Shows only what that file contributed.
Graph explorer

Browse a subject's graph; double-click an entity to pull in its neighbours. Larger circles are mentioned in more passages.

Unified pipeline in benchmarks

The API adds it with include_unified, with citation and unsupported-number rates. API only

MMemora /03 · FeaturesProduct Handbook
03 · Features

Unified Graph RAG

A second graph build reads the same chunks vector search uses, so every fact cites a real chunk. Its answers carry markers that are checked, never rewritten.

FIG 08

Unified Graph RAG

app/graphrag · build and retrieve
Purpose

Make graph evidence exactly citable and safer to answer from.

How it behaves

Facts need a verbatim quote; merges need a reason and are recorded. If evidence stays weak after widening, it abstains and lists the closest passages.

Why it matters

Answers point to specific chunks, facts and overviews; uncited sentences and unsupported numbers are flagged.

Limits

Reached only through the API (pipeline: "unified", /graph-rag/build). Measured on one small corpus; community summaries and the entity judge are not cost-metered.

Key takeaway

Builds are planned per source (new, changed, outdated, orphaned) and one run per subject holds a lease in PostgreSQL, so it works across workers.

System map

Three deployables (backend, console, public site) and the services the backend depends on. Every request is resolved to a scope by one dependency before any service runs.

FIG 11

Memora system map

left: callers · centre: backend · right, dashed: outside the repository
Key takeaway

Operations note

Slow work runs as background tasks in the API process by default; a durable job table with separate workers is a setting away.

How information is stored

PostgreSQL is the source of truth. Each stage writes its own table, so any later stage can be rebuilt without repeating the earlier ones.

FIG 13

Data in creation order

docs/data-flow.md · db/models

Three kinds of extraction output

result for API consumers, readings for chunking, content for the graph.

One cost ledger

extraction_usage records every model call, failed ones too, for extraction, graph and judge.

Derived stores repair themselves

Graph writes follow the database commit; startup sweeps clear interrupted runs and orphans.

Integrations and environments

Memora uses NVIDIA open models only: every configured model id must start with nvidia/. The environment setting decides who serves them and where files live.

local (default)production
Text models: extract, graph, answerbuild.nvidia.comNebius Token Factory
Layout, vision, embeddings, rerankerbuild.nvidia.combuild.nvidia.com (Nebius has none)
File storageLocal diskCloudflare R2

PostgreSQL + pgvector

Required. All state, vectors, lexical index and jobs.

FalkorDB

Optional. Without it, graph endpoints answer 503.

Google

Console sign-in, and Drive with a read-only scope.

Pricing file

Model prices in pricing.json turn token counts into cost.

Key takeaway

Both model providers speak the OpenAI API, so switching environments changes only configuration. Each call's cost is recorded under the provider that served it.

Trust boundaries

Three kinds of caller pass three gates into the same scope check. Behind it, every service compares a row's owners with the caller's scope.

FIG 15

Trust boundaries

Key takeaway

Cross-tenant reads return 404, not 403: a 403 would confirm the ID exists in someone else's tenant.

Known limit

A console user's scope is every tenant they own. There are no per-actor permissions inside a subject yet.

Memora Product Handbook · evidence: Memora repository @ f4c6b8c26 / 31
MMemora /07 · Security & permissionsProduct Handbook
07 · Security & permissions

Security controls

Controls verified in the backend, and the ones still missing.

Implemented

Hashed API tokens

Only an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by a server secret is stored; the raw token is shown once.

Implemented

Google-only console sign-in

ID token verified with Google; 7-day HttpOnly JWT cookie.

Implemented

Scope on every call

Ownership derived, chain checked, 404 for anything outside scope.

Implemented

Per-user Drive access

Connections are filtered by user; private mode stores nothing.

Why a keyed HMAC, not bcrypt

Authentication must find the credential from the token alone, which needs an indexed lookup; a per-row salt would force a scan. Tokens are 256 random bits, so slow hashing adds nothing, and a database dump can't forge tokens because the key never touches the database. Rotating it invalidates every credential.

Gaps found in the repository
  • Per-actor permissions inside a subject (subject_actors).Not built
  • Upload file-type allow-list.Not built
  • The session secret falls back to a placeholder if unset; set it in production.Partial
  • The README still describes a removed admin-key login.Partial

MMemora /09 · Quick referenceProduct Handbook
09 · Quick reference

Flashcards

Check your understanding. Each answer fits on one line.

Q01

What is the difference between an actor and a subject?

AThe actor caused it; the subject is the workspace.
Q02

Why does a cross-tenant read return 404?

AA 403 would confirm that the ID exists.
Q03

Which pages go to the layout model?

AHard ones: scans, tables, or many images.
Q04

Why is chunking free?

AIt runs locally on stored readings; no model call.
Q05

What makes an embedding strategy safe to change?

AIt can't change: a new setup is a new strategy.
Q06

Which two searches does a question run?

ADense HNSW and lexical tsvector, fused by RRF.
Q07

How many chunks reach the answer model?

ASix, after MMR and the reranker.
Q08

How does Graph RAG know nothing relevant was found?

AThe best rerank score is below −5.0.
Q09

What does Drive private mode keep?

ANothing: it is discarded with the answer.
Q10

Why are API tokens hashed with HMAC?

AIndexed lookup, and a dump can't forge tokens.
Q11

What happens without FalkorDB?

AGraph endpoints answer 503; the rest works.
Q12

How does Pingie use Memora?

ARetrieval only: it reads the stream's start event.

Glossary

Terms used in the console, the API and this handbook.

Tenant
The organisation that owns the data; top of the chain.
Application
A consuming system inside a tenant; holds credentials.
API credential memora_…
A token that resolves to one application.
Actor
Who or what caused something; audit only.
Subject
A workspace and data boundary; nests as folders.
Source
A registered file, URL or chat.
Extraction
A versioned reading of a source, with its cost.
Triage
Labelling each page easy, medium or hard.
Reading
One page's Markdown transcription.
Document unit
A heading, paragraph, list, table or figure.
Semantic block
Units grouped under one leaf section.
Retrieval chunk
The final piece that is embedded and searched.
Strategy
An immutable way of embedding chunks with a model.
HNSW
The approximate nearest-neighbour index in pgvector.
RRF
Reciprocal rank fusion of several ranked lists.
MMR
Maximal marginal relevance: diverse, relevant picks.
Reranker
A cross-encoder that scores question–chunk pairs.
Ontology
The allowed entity and relation types for the graph.
Graph RAG
Retrieval that uses the knowledge graph for evidence.
Arena
Console page comparing pipelines on one question.
Atomic fact
One self-contained sentence with its quote (unified).
Community
A cluster of related entities, with a summary.
Scope
What a request may see, resolved by get_scope().
Private mode
Drive Q&A with nothing stored.
